data.name: Albania
data.gender_notes: Albania is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Albania comes from the root 'alb' meaning white or light-colored, and the suffix '-an' meaning land or people. The name refers to the early inhabitants of the region who were known for their light-colored skin and hair. The name Albania carries the meaning “Land of the Eagles” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Albania usually hope their child will grow to embody land of the eagles and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Albania represents the land of spiritual awakening, a place where one can connect with nature and find inner peace and enlightenment.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Albania total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: אלבניה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלבניה, נגזר מלטינית Albania, שמקורה ביוונית אלβανία (Albanía), המתייחסת לאלבניה, ארץ באירופה. השם קשור למילה הלטינית albus, שפירושה לבן, שלג.

in_greek.name: Αλβανία
in_greek.long_meaning: Αλβανία, ονομασία που προέρχεται από την λατινική Albania, που με τη σειρά της προέρχεται από την ελληνική אלβανία (Albanía). Το όνομα πιθανόν συνδέεται με την ελληνική λέξη άλβος (alvos), που σημαίνει λευκός.

in_latin.name: Albania
in_latin.long_meaning: Albania, nomen terrae Europae, derivatum ex graeco אלבניה (Albanía) et latino Albania. Nomen probabiliter connectitur cum latino 'albus', quod significat album, niveum.

in_english.name: Albania
in_english.meaning: Land of the Albanians, white land
in_english.long_meaning: Albania, a name derived from Latin and Greek roots, refers to a country in Southeastern Europe. Etymologically, it is linked to the Latin 'albus', meaning white or snow, and the Greek 'albanos', referring to the Albanians. The name carries historical significance in Christian tradition as a nation with a rich cultural heritage.

The name has also been a rallying call for unity among the Albanian people, who have faced various challenges and adversities throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Albania can be seen as a reminder of the purity and light that exists within all of us as human beings. The name's origins in the Albanian word for white or light-colored can be interpreted as a metaphor for the pure and undamaged nature of the soul. It can also serve as a reminder of the importance of striving for inner light and enlightenment, as well as the need to protect and preserve that light within ourselves and in the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Albania, derived from the name of the first Christian King of Albanians, St. Alban, represents the courage and unwavering faith in the face of persecution. His name, meaning 'noble or kind', embodies the spirit of love and sacrifice in the face of adversity, inspiring bravery and resilience within the Albanian people.
